shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Four vanilla-matched per-level sizes (126/190/250/300) and level counts are bought from a fixed 192,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
> **NOTE TO SELF:** running spec, not a changelog. §1-19 architecture; §20 compat library; §21-22 OPEN BUGS. Keep every ⚠ - each cost a run to learn.

# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~72 files, ~20,500 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather, settings VERIFIED IN PLAY.
**NEW IN RUN #231: the 250 tier is VERIFIED IN PLAY** - `map (250, 1, 768), bands=3, slot=256`, exactly 192,000 cells, generated clean (§2).
UNVERIFIED: below-snow, depth shrink (§6g), camera anchor (§8a), the §18 audit, the reroll grid (§6d-REROLL), the VEE compat patches (§20b 1-2), the GL roof fix (§20b 4), and tiers 126/190/300.

**⚠ THREE BUGS FROM THE PUBLISHED BUILD.**
1. Preview only worked at 190x190 - **FIXED** (§6d-CLAMP). Indirectly supported by #231 (a 250 map generated and previewed), not yet explicitly confirmed at 300.
2. Fog/rocks regenerate on save reload - **NOT DIAGNOSED, HELD** (§21).
3. GL installed -> rivers show on the world map but not on the generated map - **CORE MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN PLAY** (`riverGraph: 0 node(s)`), full chain still open (§22).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight + MinGutter) / 64) * 64`; **64-alignment of SLOT is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Sizes 126 / 190 / 250 / 300.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point as a fraction of `Size.z` | river/lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a); VEE Crater jitter (§20) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on map centre | coastline (§6e); VEE LoneIsland and Crater (§20) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d); **GL landform grids (§22)** | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b/d); river WIDTH (§20) | re-base onto the cell's band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window and reroll grid (§6d); **GL `TransformIntoMapSpace` (§22)** | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar** | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16), GL roof sweep (§20) | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all `FalloffAtAngle`).

**`ABBandLocal.cs` is THE canonical FIELD rewrite** (`z' = (z % Slot) + (Size.z - bandHeight)/2`) plus `BandLocalModule`, a `ModuleBase` wrapper for consumers that sample a noise field directly. Extracted at the THIRD consumer.

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 192,000 cells

## ⚠ THE 64 CONSTRAINT IS ON *SLOT*, NOT ON BAND HEIGHT
The original tiers were all 64k-2 (126/190/254) - the *tightest* fit - and **that coincidence was mistaken for the requirement for months**, which kept vanilla's own numbers off the list.

| size | slot | gutter | cells/band | playable | max levels | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 126 | 128 | 2 | 16,128 | 98.4% | 7 (cap) | 112,896 |
| 190 | 192 | 2 | 36,480 | 99.0% | 5 | 182,400 |
| **250** | 256 | 6 | 64,000 | 97.7% | 3 | **192,000** ✅ VERIFIED #231 |
| **300** | 320 | 20 | 96,000 | 93.8% | 2 | **192,000** |

250 and 300 are vanilla's Medium and Large exactly. **The budget is tuned:** 192,000 is simultaneously `3 x 64,000` and `2 x 96,000`; `6 x 190`, `4 x 250`, `3 x 300` are refused. Ladder 7/5/3/2, monotone, every tier yields real z-levels - which is why 350 and 382 are not offered (a second level costs more than the whole budget).

**⚠ 200 IS THE ONE NUMBER TO AVOID.** Just past the 192 boundary: slot 256, gutter 56, 21.9% wasted. **Waste is a SAWTOOTH.** Recompute the table before adding a size.

**⚠ A WIDE GUTTER IS A FEATURE.** "A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter" is the root of §15a and §4. Gutter is 6 rows at 250, 20 at 300.

**Old saves are safe.** `bandHeight` is scribed per map; `SlotFor` is generic.

Per-level size is SQUARE, so `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` already yields a per-BAND count. **Squareness is a repair tool:** `Size.x == bandHeight`.

**⚠ THE PLAN PERSISTS BETWEEN COLONIES, AND IT SILENTLY CONSTRAINS THE SIZE.** Confirmed again in #231: the first map generated `7 bands of 126 | 3 up / 3 down` when 250/3 was intended. Nothing is broken - at 7 levels 250 costs 448,000 against a 192,000 budget, so the chooser correctly greys it out. **The levels must be reduced BEFORE the larger size becomes selectable.** Read the PLAN line of the profile before believing any size test.

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play. Our radio buttons write `GameInitData.mapSize` directly - **which is why it is the authoritative record of the player's choice, and why nothing should re-derive it (§6d-CLAMP).** Window grown via `InitialSize` postfix; **adding a tier means growing that number** (now +288f).
**⚠ The chooser LATCHES global state, released in a `Finalizer`** (§18a).

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof: only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band. TEN systems share it. **EIGHT appearances of the single `- Slot` bug** (the eighth written as INDEX arithmetic so the standing `grep '- Slot'` audit could not see it).
**`TryResolveVisibleFrom` is THE gate** - folds the four-question preamble onto the descent. Two legitimate exceptions: `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` needs the "in bounds but fogged" distinction; the upward-shape consumers ask a different question and translate before descending.
Sun shadows: mask and descent answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, smallest drop among nine cells.

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts on record. Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.**
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS A SET OF MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` is a port of vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Every other vanilla pass needs its own mirror. Confirmed twice: Water (§6b), Snow (§6f).
Mirrors: BelowV2, BelowLighting, BelowShadows, BelowEdgeShadows, BelowWatergen, BelowSnow, MountainCap.

**⚠ THE CONVERSE IS ALREADY HANDLED.** A foreign `Thing.Print` postfix prints into OUR layer and is still correct, because the call is bracketed `SnapshotVertCounts()` -> `t.Print(this)` -> `FinishNewVerts(...)` and **`FinishNewVerts` transforms by VERTEX RANGE, not by knowing which graphic emitted what**. Preserve that property.

**Cross-band invalidation: `Patch_MapDrawer_ABMirrorDirtyUp`, with an ASCENT RULE** - stops at the first opaque floor, tested over the cell AND its eight neighbours. The FIRST step stays unconditional (MountainCap derives from exactly one Slot below). Mirrors vanilla's `ProgramState != Playing` guard.
**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.**

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples the WaterDepth subcamera's texture at its own SCREEN position. `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
Rivers: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately); `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first. Width clamped at the producer (§20b).
**⚠ ALL THREE OF THOSE ARE DEAD WHEN GL IS INSTALLED - CONFIRMED IN PLAY, §22.**

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP (verified)
ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW
Never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` - a bare Map plus a short genstep list on a background thread, so our banding prefix never fires. **Generate at full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`.** `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise.

## 6d-CLAMP. ⚠ THE PUBLISHED BUG: PREVIEW ONLY WORKED AT 190x190 (FIXED)
`Stacked()` ran the incoming size through `Clamp()`, which returns *the largest offered size ≤ input that fits at the current level count*. Map Preview passes VANILLA's configured size (250 default), not our pick:
```
Clamp(250) at 4 levels -> 190   ->  lastBandHeight = 190
TryBandRows: BandCount * SlotFor(190) == stackedZ ?  only true if 190 was chosen
```
**Fix: `ABMapSizeLimit.PlannedSize`.** `Clamp` answers "sanitise DOWN to something affordable" and is LOSSY by design; it was being used to answer "what did the player choose?" - which was never a derivation problem, since the chooser writes `GameInitData.mapSize` directly.
Also fixed: `Stacked` clamped x and z INDEPENDENTLY though a band is square; `FixWindowAspect` re-Clamped `lastBandHeight`.

**⚠ MAP PREVIEW SHIPS IN TWO HALVES, AND GL BUNDLES ONE.** The engine half is byte-identical in both. But `MapPreviewWindow` and `MapSeedRerollWindow` live ONLY in `MapPreviewMod.dll`, which GL does not ship. **With GL installed and Map Preview absent, `Active` is TRUE while the window types are ABSENT.** Safe only because every target is null-guarded independently. **Do not "simplify" `Active` into a single gate.**

## 6d-REROLL (UNVERIFIED)
**⚠ The window opened COMPLETELY EMPTY:** `elementSize.y = 403/126*896 = 2,866 px` -> `gridSize.y = 0` -> `DesiredCount = 0` -> trim loop disposes everything and `TryAddElement` returns immediately. **The SECOND consumer of the stacked size caught out by it.** Fixed by a postfix re-deriving `_elementSize.y` from the BAND height. A POSTFIX repairing two statics, not a reimplementation.

# 6e. COASTS (verified)
CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. NO SCALING - stretching band-local z skews non-axis-aligned fields and makes displacement noise anisotropic.
**⚠ "None override `GetNoiseValue`" is about VANILLA ONLY.** VEE's LoneIsland declares its own and drowns the colony (§20).

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (UNVERIFIED)
**No mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed.** The near-miss that hid it: `CellTerrainAt` genuinely samples `snowGrid.GetDepth(below)`, but that value is consumed only by `MaterialFor` to pick the POLLUTED variant - the right value read for an entirely different purpose.
Geometry built once and reused (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry`; empty cells still emit nine transparent vertices; all nine kernel samples at the CENTRE cell's drop.
**⚠ Draw ordering is queue-decided.** `MatBases.Snow` may need queue work.

# 6g. DEPTH SHRINK (UNVERIFIED)
Exponent is the accumulated drop (three levels down = 61%). Baked at print time.
- **⚠ The atlas trap:** past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Verification must cross that boundary in both directions.**
- Right-multiply the pawn matrix; a left multiply slides every below pawn towards the map origin.
- **⚠ Exclusion filter kept verbatim:** LINKED graphics print one quad per cell; natural rock excluded BY DEF, because Better Mountains swaps rock to non-linked `Graphic_Random` wholesale.
- **ReGrowth does NOT contest this** - its transpiler hits `Graphic_Linked.Print` + 3 subclasses, no-op unless `printingSnow`, and we already exclude linked graphics.

**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add as polish.** Correct and cheap, cut because the shrink alone carried the depth read and perspective bought a second cue at the price of a real artifact.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, caves `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, after the settings clamp. **The ore multiplier scales `basementOreDensity` through our OWN `ABOreGen.ScatterOres`** - not `countPer10kCellsRange`.
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.**
Climate: +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement -6, wind x1.15/1.30/1.50.

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL. **The clamp and level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`**, both on per-frame paths where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into a hang.

# 8a. NEW-GAME CAMERA ANCHOR (UNVERIFIED)
Two things move the colony AFTER `PlayerStartSpot` is chosen: `RescueStrandedColonists` and the carve. Fixed upstream + backstop; **only `StartedNewGame` runs after vanilla's own camera jump.**
**⚠ OPEN:** `z=24` was EXACTLY `PodScatterMargin`. Vanilla's pick and my clamp look identical from outside.

# 9. GENERATION COST

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, `SCOPING:` and two censuses. It has now voided or explained five comparisons, including #231's plan mismatch. Emitted at WARNING deliberately.
**⚠ THE WATER REPORT DOES NOT DO THIS AND SHOULD.** In #231 the water report gave a clean answer for a map whose TILE and MUTATORS it never printed, so it cannot be compared against the profile from a different generation. **Add TILE + mutators + PLAN to `ABWaterBand.Report`.**

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION - *NO LONGER TRUE, AND THE FIX IS WHY*
Run #188: gensteps 3,972 ms, carve 20,447 ms, 74,584 destroyed. Generation 16%, destruction 84%.
**⚠ RUN #231 INVERTS THIS: gensteps 3,836 ms (71%), carve 1,580 ms (29%), 4,575 destroyed.** Rock suppression worked, so the carve got cheap and the remaining cost moved to generation. **The 16/84 ratio is now a historical record of a fixed problem, not a current fact. Do not plan against it.**

## 9c. The culprit was rock, proven by census
#190: 43,517 rock SUPPRESSED vs 4,939 DESTROYED of which only 238 rock. Stable across four tiles.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` in `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` for doomed SKY cells. Safe by **shape**, **state-neutrality**, **sky only**.

## 9e. The basement is the remaining carve cost
#196 FillRock bands 0-2 = 2,606 ms (82% of carve). #231: 926 ms of a 1,580 ms carve (59%).
**⚠ MY OWN §9d CAUTION IS FALSIFIED.** The basement keep hits only **14.4%**; suppressing trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 spawns (~200 ms). **Net ~1.2 s.**
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` INVERTED (rising with altitude), because rock tapers upward so higher bands have more OPEN ground and chunks only grow on open ground. Seen again in #231 (193/170/193 ms, flat).

## 9f. ⚠ EVERY ABSOLUTE TIMING HERE PREDATES THE TIER CHANGE
A 3 x 250 colony is 192,000 cells against 7 x 126's 112,896 - 1.7x - and cost tracks cell count. Re-baseline before comparing across it.

## 9g. ⚠ NEW #1 CANDIDATE: `GenStep_Plants` IN DOOMED BANDS
Run #231, `7 x 126` on TropicalSwamp:
```
2270.1 ms  GenStep - Plants     <- 59% of ALL genstep time
 358.0 ms  GenStep - Terrain
 293.8 ms  GenStep - MutatorPostTerrain
3835.7 ms  all gensteps
1580.1 ms  AB band carve
```
Six of seven bands are doomed (95,256 of 112,896 cells), so **~84% of that 2,270 ms is vegetation generated and immediately erased**. Exactly the shape §9d already solves for rock: suppress the spawn, do not redistribute a count.
**⚠ n=1, AND ON THE HIGHEST-PLANT-DENSITY BIOME IN THE GAME.** The mechanism is tile-independent; the magnitude is not. Confirm on a second biome before ranking it above the basement work.

### Ranked
1. **`GenStep_Plants` doomed-band suppression** (~1.9 s on #231's tile, unconfirmed elsewhere).
2. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e), ~1.2 s.
3. **`GenStep_RockChunks`** - `Filth_RubbleRock` was still the top destroyed def in #231 (2,462 of 4,575).
4. **Scattered ruins, also a CONTENT BUG** - count sized for ONE band, placement spans the stack, so the surface loses ruins vanilla intended.
5. **`ABRockGen.PickIndex` 6-octave Perlin per cell.** NOT DONE: changes determinism.

# 10, 11. PERF
59.6 fps at 96 pawns. **⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING** - cost is concentrated in section-regeneration BURSTS. Any perf claim needs a mining/construction test with a multi-level plan.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** #172 opened with a stale `belowWater=False` that mimicked a fixed bug exactly. Now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.**
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always strips its LAST entry.** `EnsureAllNodesValid` walks BACKWARDS while `GetNode` is still lazily building the graph. **Now n=4** - #231 lost the deliberate `AB2: camera calibration` padding and kept all three real instruments. **The padding trick is confirmed; keep using a DISTINCT throwaway last.**
`AB2: band info` is the fastest ground truth for what a map actually generated as.

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **§22 GL rivers** - run the DISCRIMINATING config (levels BELOW surface). §231 could not discriminate.
2. **§21 fog/rocks on reload** - the two-question observation.
3. **§9g plants** - confirm on a second biome, then implement.
4. Verify tiers 126/190/300 and the preview fix explicitly at 300.
5. Verify the §18 audit, VEE compat (§20b 1-2), GL roof fix (§20b 4), reroll grid, depth shrink, camera anchor, below-snow.
6. Stamp TILE/PLAN into the water report (§9a).
7. Basement rock suppression; §9g 4-5; audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators.
8. **Never exercised:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, basement PATHING/wormholes, cavern basement (§18e).
9. Below-pawn drawing serial and cache-disabled; realtime-things pass single-band and unshrunk.
10. `ShotReport` cross-band accuracy drops target size. Biomes! at 40%. **Store page still says three levels.**

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. Re-open a rejection only by naming the confound. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. A beautiful fit is not evidence.
**⚠ CHECK THAT YOUR CONFIGURATION CAN EXPRESS THE DIFFERENCE BEFORE RUNNING THE EXPERIMENT.** #231's water report was clean, unambiguous, and **worthless as a discriminator**: with `0 down / 2 up`, `surfaceBand = 0`, so "the river lands in band 0" (my bug model) and "the river lands on the surface" (no bug) are THE SAME SENTENCE. A discriminating experiment needs a configuration where the hypotheses *disagree*; here that means `surfaceBand > 0`. **Write down what each hypothesis predicts for THIS setup before you run it, and if the predictions match, change the setup.**
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed** - and **re-measure after you fix it**. Generation was 16% and is now 71% (§9b), because the fix worked. A ratio is a snapshot of a moment, not a property of the system.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.**
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output.** Five comparisons saved. **And apply it to EVERY diagnostic, not just the one that taught you** - the water report still lacks it (§9a).
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence; the discriminating experiment is usually cheap.**
**⚠ THE SYMPTOM SET IS ITSELF EVIDENCE - ask what the affected things SHARE.** In §21 the report named fog AND rocks and nothing else: precisely the two things stored as flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`. Everything else is saved individually.
**⚠ An optimisation you declined for a stated reason still owes you the number.**
**⚠ A correct value read for the wrong purpose looks like coverage.**
**⚠ Aim at the fact, not at the record of the intent.** `GameInitData.mapSize` IS the player's choice.
**⚠ A LOSSY NORMALISER IS NOT A WAY TO READ A CHOICE.** `Clamp` was right at its own job and wrong as an answer to "what did the user pick?" **When a function's contract is "snap to something valid", it can never RECOVER a value.**
**⚠ A CONSTRAINT SATISFIED BY EVERY EXAMPLE IS NOT NECESSARILY THE CONSTRAINT.** All three original sizes were 64k-2, read for months as a requirement; the real rule was only that *Slot* is 64-aligned. **Derive the constraint from the mechanism, not from the set of things you already built.**
**⚠ THE REAL CONFLICT IS USUALLY A REPLACEMENT, NOT A COLLISION.** Every §20 candidate was "we both patch X". The bug that shipped broken (§22) is the opposite: GL *substitutes its own worker*, so our patches never run. **A patch that is silently never invoked produces no error, no log line, no conflict warning.** `riverGraph: 0 node(s)` is what that looks like from the outside. **Ask what a mod REPLACES, not only what it patches.**
**⚠ A SHARED METHOD NAME IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT A CONFLICT.** Name-matching false-positive rate was 50%. ReGrowth cleared four separate times.
**⚠ Compat work is mostly deletion.** 150 mutators produced 2 patches.
**⚠ Design for the foreign patch you have not met.** `FinishNewVerts` transforms a VERTEX RANGE, so foreign print injection is correct for free.
**⚠ Waste is often a sawtooth, not a curve.** **⚠ The thing you rounded away may be load-bearing** - wide gutters are the cheapest defence against seam-crossing.
**⚠ A rule enforced by grepping for a SYNTAX only catches that syntax.** **⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** **⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** **⚠ A kill switch with no call site is noise.** **⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** **⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return.** **⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** **⚠ A finding scoped to vanilla does not transfer to mods.**
**Patching.** Re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through - and when there is none, **wrap the DATA instead of the reader**. Patch the PRODUCER, not the store. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch signature - type `__instance` as `object`. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **Prefix state is released in a Finalizer, never a Postfix.** **Mirror the guard of the method you postfix.** **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing it.** **Never clamp a Def field to fix one map.** **Prefer a published ExtensionPoint over racing internals.**
**Engine facts.** `holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order is material render QUEUE, not altitude. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. `Banded` is FALSE for all of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered on EVERY map. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread - generation latches must be `[ThreadStatic]`. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` and `MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` both return silently unless `ProgramState == Playing`. Humanlikes past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit ignoring `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED (~40x cheaper than after `FinalizeInit`).** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws but always runs FINALIZERS; **a prefix returning false skips the original but POSTFIXES STILL RUN**; a prefix and a transpiler compose. **`FogGrid` and compressible things are flat per-cell arrays sized by `map.Area`; everything else saves individually.** **`WaterInfo.GetWaterMovement` indexes `x * map.Size.z + z` (x-major).** **TileMutatorDefs compete within a `categories` entry, so a mod can REPLACE a vanilla mutator by declaring its own in the same category.**

---

# 15. QOL PASS (verified, #172)
**15a. Nothing may exist in the void.** Finders answer inside the surface band; a `GenSpawn.Spawn` prefix rewrites `loc`; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves.
**15b. Structures must not straddle a seam.** `CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases onto the band rect; eleven cold call sites inherit it.
**⚠ ONE surface-edge finder.** A null dir means "any side, re-rolled every attempt" - deliberately, because a validator that rejects a whole side must not trap the search.
**15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge REMOVED** - consequence: vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge.
**15e. Drop pods fall through the levels.**

# 16. ALTITUDE AND WEATHER (verified)
- `AB_OpenAir` / `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`.
- Melt per band: prefix on `DoCellSteadyEffects` rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call. **ReGrowth transpiles the same method; prefix and transpiler compose.**
- Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def shared across maps.
- **Readout:** rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. `MapTemperature.OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached, because outdoor cells still belong to a Room and `Room.Temperature` is a stored field.

# 17. SETTINGS PASS (verified)
**⚠ The blank-tab bug.** Content height from the previous frame's `CurHeight` is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH without a floor. Fix: `Mathf.Max(list.CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`.
**⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.**
**The unlock gate:** the checkbox writes to a LOCAL; the stored value IS the record that the warning was read.

# 22. ⚠ GEOLOGICAL LANDFORMS SUPPRESSES RIVERS - CORE MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN PLAY

## Established, and now CONFIRMED IN PLAY (#231)
**GL REPLACES vanilla river generation - it does not patch it.** `GL_River`, `GL_RiverConfluence`, `GL_RiverDelta`, `GL_RiverIsland`, `GL_RiverSource`, `GL_RiverTerrain` are `TileMutatorDef`s in the **`River` category** built on `TileMutatorWorker_Landform`. Mutators compete within a category, so GL's win and vanilla's worker never runs.

**#231 proves it directly: `riverGraph: 0 node(s)` on a `GL_RiverConfluence, GL_RiverTerrain` tile.** Vanilla's `GenerateRiverGraph` never populated it. **Every river patch we own is therefore inert under GL** - §6b `GetRiverCenter`, `GetLakeCenter`, and §20b's width clamp. They do not conflict; **they are never invoked**, which is why this produced no error and no log line.

GL's river runs through:
```
Landform.OutputWaterFlow.GetRiverTerrain()
  -> Landform.TransformIntoMapSpace(...)
  -> ApplyBuffered(map.Size, TerrainAt, SetTerrain)   // terrain
  -> ApplyWaterFlow(map)                              // waterInfo.riverFlowMap
```

## ⚠ #231 DID NOT DISCRIMINATE, AND THE REASON MATTERS
Water report on `map (250, 1, 768), bands=3, surfaceBand=0`:
```
band 0 (level 0): water=13518  withDepthMat=13518  baseRiver=13115
band 1 (level 1): water=0
band 2 (level 2): water=0
```
The river is present and rendering with the depth material. **But `surfaceBand = 0` (0 down / 2 up), so band 0 IS the surface** - and my bug model predicts the river lands in band 0 (node grid rows 0-249). **Both hypotheses predict exactly this output.** The run is clean, correct, and worthless as a discriminator.

**⚠ THE DISCRIMINATING CONFIG IS `surfaceBand > 0`** - any levels BELOW the surface. With `1 down / 1 up` at 250: band 0 = basement (rows 0-249), band 1 = surface (rows 256-505).
- **Bug model:** water in band 0 (BASEMENT), band 1 (surface) = 0. -> §22 reproduces.
- **No bug:** water in band 1.

**This also explains the original report.** The default plan is 1 up / 1 down (`surfaceBand = 1`), so a normal player has the surface at band 1 and the river lands in the basement - "rivers never appear on the map", exactly as reported. #231 happened to use the one plan shape where the bug is invisible.
